rationale: Both candidates miss the literal GT asks (3-way perf benchmark, extract-to-shared-util) but independently converge on a deeper version of the shared-util concern by finding the 'shared' helper has only one caller while two identical BNSD sites remain unguarded, and both correctly diagnose that the changed test's shape is rejected by D-alignment rather than the B*N<=S*8 predicate it's meant to cover, plus the non-contiguous return. X backs its claims with denser, cross-checked evidence (e.g. validating its concurrency-threshold math against the PR's own stated 'concurrency>=4' trigger, and a careful CI-collection check before flagging the AMD failure) and adds two well-grounded extra findings (310P fp16 arch gating, AMD CI scope) that Y lacks. Y's parallel 'unmigrated call site' claim uses a first-AR-step scenario that would imply crashes at much lower concurrency than the PR's own passing benchmarks suggest, making it less internally consistent, though Y contributes one genuinely unique, solid finding (uncited/version-coupled CANN tiling constant) and slightly cleaner inline-diff actionability.
